View doc summary

Connect Gladly AI to an external MCP server so it can call that server's tools during Customer conversations. This article covers adding and testing a connection, then using its tools in a Guide. To learn how MCP connections work, see What are MCP connections?

> MCP tools reach Gladly AI only after you add them to a Guide or Skill.
> 
> Replies that use MCP tool data pass the same reply guardrails as any other Gladly AI reply.

## Before you begin

Have the following ready for the MCP server you want to connect:

  * The server URL, for example `https://api.example.com/mcp`

  * The type of authentication the server uses: none, bearer token, API key, or OAuth (authorization code or client credentials)

  * The credentials for that authentication type

## Access MCP settings

  1. Go to Settings.

  2. Under App Developer Tools, select MCP.

The MCP page lists your connections on the Active and Inactive tabs. For each connection, the table shows the connection name, the server, its success rate, and its status.

MCP page with no connections configured.

If you haven't added a connection yet, the page prompts you to add one.

Image

## Add a connection to a new MCP server

  1. On the MCP page, select Add Connection.

  2. Select the Server dropdown, then select +

View doc summary

An MCP connection links Gladly AI to an external system so it can look up information or take action during a Customer Conversation. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI systems discover and call the tools an external system offers. With an MCP connection, Gladly AI can check an order status, search a product catalog, or look up store hours while it helps a customer, using live data from your own systems.

## How MCP connections work

When a customer asks a question, Gladly AI decides whether one of your MCP tools can help. If it can, Gladly AI calls the tool on your MCP server, reads the response, and uses it to answer the customer.

For example, a customer asks, "Where is my order RT-1001?" The Custom Action calls the MCP tool as one of its steps, and you control what the Action collects from the customer and what it passes to the tool. MCP tools work alongside your other Actions, so a single Guide can use both.

See Set up MCP connections for the steps.

## Authentication options

Gladly supports the following authentication types for an MCP server:

  * None

  * Bearer Token

  * API Key

  * OAuth (Authorization Code)

  * OAuth (Client Credentials)

Use the type your server requires. If you're not sure which one to use, ask the team that manages the server.

pages.title: Generate API Tokens and Create Webhooks (https://help.gladly.com/generate-api-tokens-and-create-webhooks)
pages.text: Generate API Tokens and Create Webhooks Documentation Index Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://help.gladly.com/llms.txt Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further. Generate API Tokens and Create Webhooks Updated on Feb 13, 2025 Published on Jan 30, 2025 4 minute(s) read Focus Listen Print Copy page Copy as Markdown for LLMs View as Markdown View the page as plain text Open in ChatGPT Ask ChatGPT about this page Open in Claude Ask Claude about this page View doc summary Prev Next REQUIRED USER ROLE API User PERMISSION OVERVIEW View permissions by role API tokens are required to use Gladly APIs for security and authentication purposes. Tokens can be accessed and created by users who at least have an API user role . Before you start For integrations not built by Gladly, a Gladly Administrator should create a new user with an API role + Agent and/or Administrator (check with your integration partner to confirm the required roles) account for each integration. This account should be used to access Gladly to create the API tokens or webhooks. The integration partner should provide the email address to be used with the integration's user account in Gladly. They must also access emails from this account to activate their Gladly account to create API tokens or webhooks. API tokens are tied to a single user account and a particular environment. For example, an API token attached to Gladly user developer@customer.com in the Sandbox environment is not valid for developer@customer.com in the Production environment. We recommend creating a dedicated Gladly user to make API calls whose account won't be used for Agent and organization management. This will help you with any future audits of API activity vs. Agent activity. Create a unique user account linked to webhooks or tokens As an Administrator, create a user to use explicitly to create and attach webhooks or tokens. Be sure to add the user with at least an API User role + Agent and/or Administrator. If this user needs access to reports, they'll need Administrator access. For a complete list of user permissions, click here . Note – We recommend creating a dedicated user to make API calls. Use the email address provided by the integration partner if you're given one. Use a name to help you quickly identify the integration user. For example, "Retale Integration." An email will be sent to the user. Someone must complete the registration and sign in to Gladly to create API tokens or webhooks. They'll have 24 hours to accept the user invitation before it expires. See How do I reset my password for login issues. For SSO users, see Manager Users through SSO for more information. Deactivating an API User If a user account with API tokens or webhooks attached to it is deactivated, apps or external sources using the token or webhook linked to the user will stop working. Create API tokens Click on the top left corner of the screen. Click Settings . Under the App Developer Tools category, click API tokens . The API tokens page will show you a list of currently available API tokens. Click Create Token . A new token is immediately generated within the page. Copy and secure the token under the Token column. The token is only shown once , so save it in a secure location. Click the token name (e.g., Token 1) to rename the token to make it easy to identify how the token is used. To delete a token, hover over the token and click . Create new webhooks Create up to 50 webhooks for your organization. See our developer guide for more information about webhooks. Click on the top left corner of the screen. Click Settings . Under the App Developer Tools category, click Webhooks . The Webhooks page will show you a list of webhooks you currently have configured. Click Create Webhook . From the Create Webhook page, enter the following information: Name – Enter a name to help you identify the app using a webhook. Enabled (toggle) – Allows you to activate/deactivate the webhook. Click the toggle so it's green to activate the webhook. Webhook URL – Enter the URL where you'd like to send events. If you get an "unable to ping URL" error, double-check the URL and make sure it's correct. Events – Select the events you'd like to use from the search picklist. The Webhook Events you select are added below the search bar. For more information about Webhook Events, please visit our developer guide . Username (Optional) – Enter the username for the app you are integrating. Password (Optional) – Enter the password for the app you are integrating. Realm (Optional) – Enter realm to run basic auth against. HTTP Headers (Optional) – There are two columns (Header, Value) required for HTTP Headers (e.g., X-API-Key) to be included in every request. Click Add a Header to add a new line. Click to delete a line. Click Save . This will take you back to the Webhooks page, where the webhook you just added is visible. Activate/Deactivate a webhook In the Status column, click the toggle next to the webhook you want to activate/deactivate. The toggle turns gray when it's deactivated and green when activated. Reactivate a webhook Gladly automatically deactivates webhooks that fail. To see when a webhook was deactivated, hover over the exclamation point . Once the issue causing the webhook to fail is resolved, reactivate it. If the webhook is not being used, keep it deactivated or delete it if it is no longer used. Delete a webhook To delete a webhook, hover over the webhook and click . Replace or rotate API tokens Should you lose this token or wish to rotate your application keys, you can do the following: Generate a new token. Store the new token in a secure location. Delete the old token. Update your applications/scripts with the new token. Was this doc helpful? Set up MCP connections Published on Nov 12, 2026 7 minute(s) read Focus Listen Print Copy page Copy as Markdown for LLMs View as Markdown View the page as plain text Open in ChatGPT Ask ChatGPT about this page Open in Claude Ask Claude about this page View doc summary Prev Next Connect Gladly AI to an external MCP server so it can call that server's tools during Customer conversations. This article covers adding and testing a connection, then using its tools in a Guide. To learn how MCP connections work, see What are MCP connections? MCP tools reach Gladly AI only after you add them to a Guide or Skill. Replies that use MCP tool data pass the same reply guardrails as any other Gladly AI reply. Before you begin Have the following ready for the MCP server you want to connect: The server URL, for example https://api.example.com/mcp The type of authentication the server uses: none, bearer token, API key, or OAuth (authorization code or client credentials) The credentials for that authentication type Access MCP settings Go to Settings . Under App Developer Tools , select MCP . The MCP page lists your connections on the Active and Inactive tabs. For each connection, the table shows the connection name, the server, its success rate, and its status. MCP page with no connections configured. If you haven't added a connection yet, the page prompts you to add one. Add a connection to a new MCP server On the MCP page, select Add Connection . Select the Server dropdown, then select + New MCP server . Enter the Server URL . Enter a Server name that helps your team recognize the server, for example "Retalè Footwear". Select an Authentication type: None Bearer Token API Key OAuth (Authorization Code) OAuth (Client Credentials) Enter the credentials for the authentication type you selected. For OAuth (Authorization Code), a sign-in window opens so you can authorize the connection. (Optional) Enter a Description , for example "Store information, order status lookups, and product catalog search". Enter a Connection name , for example "retale-footwear". Keep Active turned on if you want the connection available right away. Select Save . When the connection is saved, the Connection Added page confirms that the connection is saved. Select Test Tools to try one of the server's tools right away, or select Done to return to the MCP page. Add another connection to an existing server If your org already has a server registered, you can create another connection to it, for example to use different credentials. On the MCP page, select Add Connection . Select the Server dropdown and choose a server under Your servers . You can search by name or URL. Enter a Connection name . Keep Active turned on if you want the connection available right away. Select Save . Test the MCP You have two test options: Test Connection checks that Gladly can reach the server and find its tools, and Test Tool runs one tool so you can review its output. What is a tool? In MCP, a tool is a single action an external server lets Gladly AI run, such as looking up an order or searching a product catalog. Each tool has a name, a description, and the inputs it needs, and it returns a result that Gladly AI can use in its reply. One MCP server can offer many tools, and Gladly discovers them automatically when you add a connection. Examples from a footwear store’s server: lookup_order_status : takes an order number and returns the order’s status and tracking details. search_products : takes a search phrase, such as “loafers”, and returns matching products with prices and sizes. get_store_hours : takes no inputs and returns the store’s hours. Test a connection Test a connection to confirm that Gladly can reach the server and discover its tools. On the MCP page, select the menu at the end of the connection's row. Select Test Connection . A confirmation banner appears with the number of tools Gladly found on the server, for example "Connected - 3 tools available". Test a tool Run a tool on its own to see what it returns, before you add it to a Guide or Skill. On the MCP page, select the menu at the end of the connection's row, then select Test Tool . Select the Tool dropdown and choose the tool you want to run. You can search the list by name. Run stays unavailable until you select a tool. Review the tool's description and the Input schema at the bottom of the page. Required fields are marked REQUIRED . Select Required only to hide optional fields, or Copy to copy the schema. Fill in the fields. For inputs that aren't simple text, such as arrays, select Edit as JSON . If the tool takes no inputs, an Arguments (JSON) box appears with {} in it. Leave it as is. Select Run . The result appears under Run , labeled Success when the call works. Select Copy to copy the result. If you leave a required field empty, the tool call fails. Check the Input schema to confirm which fields the tool requires. Manage the MCP View tool call logs Tool call logs show each time a tool ran, including test runs. On the MCP page, select the menu at the end of the connection's row. Select View Logs . Select a log entry to expand it. Each entry shows the tool name, the date and time of the call, and a green check mark if the call succeeded. Select the Request tab to see the request URL, method, header keys, and payload. Select the Response tab to see the response information, header keys, and body. The time the call took appears at the top right. Edit, deactivate, or delete a connection From the menu at the end of a connection's row, you can: Select Edit to update the connection. Select Deactivate to take the connection offline without deleting it. Deactivated connections move to the Inactive tab. Select Delete to remove the connection. Use MCP tools in conversations To make an MCP tool available to Gladly AI in a Guide, wrap the tool in a Custom Action , then add that Action to a Guide section. The Custom Action calls the MCP tool as one of its steps. The examples below use a product search tool, search_products , on a faux company MCP server. Create a Custom Action that calls an MCP tool Create a Custom Action Go to Settings . Under App Developer Tools , select Custom Actions . Select Add App Action . Enter a Name and a Description . Gladly uses these to decide when to run the Action, so describe what the Action does, what input it needs, and what it returns. Under Inputs , select Add and enter the information Gladly AI needs to collect from the customer: Name: A descriptive name in snake_case or camelCase, for example query . Description: What the input represents and how it should be formatted, for example "The customer's shoe search, such as a style, color, or category (loafers, boots, sneakers, sandals)". Type: Select the data type, for example String . Input required: Select this if the Action can't run without the input. Add (+ icon) and configure a Tool step: Name: A name for the step in snake_case or camelCase, for example searchProducts . Configuration: Select your MCP connection. Tool: Select the MCP tool to run. The tool's description appears below the dropdown. Required Parameters: Map each tool parameter to an Action input by entering $.params. followed by the input name. For example, enter $.params.query for the query parameter. Select Save . New Actions are saved as Inactive . Test the Action In the Action editor, select Test . In the Test inputs window, optionally imitate a customer, set the Channel Type , set Is Authenticated , and enter a Gladly Agent ID or Conversation ID . Enter a value for each Action input, for example "boots" for query . Select Test . Set the Action to active An Action must be active before you can use it in a Guide. On the Custom Actions page, select the Inactive tab. Select the menu at the end of the Action's row, then select Set to active . In the Set as active window, select Set as active . Any recent changes are saved and become available in Guides and App Actions. From the same menu, you can select Edit , View logs , or Duplicate . Apply the Action to a Guide Add the Custom Action to a Guide Open your AI Agent, then select Add Guide , or open an existing Guide. Enter a name and a short description for the Guide. In a section, enter a heading and a description of when to use it, for example "Use this when a customer asks about shoes, styles, colors, sizes, prices, or availability." Keep Action selected, then select the Select Action dropdown. You can search by name. Select your Action. It appears in the list with a Read tag. In Tell Gladly what to do and where to go next , enter the steps Gladly AI should follow. Tell Gladly AI to always run the Action first, and tell it which results to share. Select Save and make sure the Guide is Active . Test the Guide in Chat In the Guide, select Test . Select the Chat channel. Send a message that matches the section, for example "Do you have loafers?" Gladly AI runs the Action, the Action calls the MCP tool, and Gladly AI replies with the data the tool returned. If you added product cards, they appear above the reply. To confirm the call happened, open View Logs for the connection on the MCP page. Troubleshoot a Guide that doesn't call the Action If Gladly AI answers from other content instead of running the Action, check the following: Confirm the Action is active and the Guide is saved and active. Tell Gladly AI to always run the Action in the section instructions, as in the example above. Review other Guides and Knowledge sources that describe the same topic. Conflicting content can take priority over the Guide. Deactivate or update it, then test again. Use MCP tools with other Actions A single Guide can use MCP tools and other Actions together. For example, one section can search products with an MCP tool, and another can check an order with an App Platform Action. For more on how MCP connections behave, including what happens when a server is unreachable, see What are MCP connections? Customer or C ustomers refers to the people you support through Gladly who buy or use your products or services. Was this doc helpful? Yes No Previous doc What are MCP connections? Environment Access Published on Jan 30, 2025 1 minute(s) read Focus Listen Print Copy page Copy as Markdown for LLMs View as Markdown View the page as plain text Open in ChatGPT Ask ChatGPT about this page Open in Claude Ask Claude about this page View doc summary Prev Next Background At the beginning of your implementation, Gladly will assign you a unique subdomain. This subdomain will typically correspond with your company name. For example, Acme, Inc. would be assigned acme as its subdomain. On production, this will look like acme.gladly.com . If your implementation package contains access to a sandbox environment, it will look like acme.gladly.qa on sandbox. When Gladly sets up an environment, it will come with these default settings . Goals The purpose of this step is to give you and your project team access to Gladly as soon as possible. This will enable you to complete the next parts of the project. Estimated Effort None, beyond logging into Gladly! Step-by-Step Tutorial & Best Practices Let your implementation team know during kickoff which emails to grant access to. Your implementation team will set them up as administrators with API access on Gladly. For customers who have both sandbox and production, we will grant access to both environments. We recommend keeping to the project team only until you are ready for agent training. You will receive an invite to your email inbox. Accept the invite within 24 hours. Let your implementation team know if you have not received an invite, or need it resent. Was this doc helpful? pages.title: What are MCP connections? (https://help.gladly.com/docs/what-are-mcp-connections)
pages.text: What are MCP connections? Documentation Index Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://help.gladly.com/llms.txt Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further. What are MCP connections? Updated on Nov 12, 2026 Published on Nov 7, 2026 3 minute(s) read Focus Listen Print Copy page Copy as Markdown for LLMs View as Markdown View the page as plain text Open in ChatGPT Ask ChatGPT about this page Open in Claude Ask Claude about this page View doc summary Prev Next An MCP connection links Gladly AI to an external system so it can look up information or take action during a Customer Conversation . MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI systems discover and call the tools an external system offers. With an MCP connection, Gladly AI can check an order status, search a product catalog, or look up store hours while it helps a customer, using live data from your own systems. Instead of building a custom App Platform integration for every external system, you register an MCP server once. Gladly discovers the tools on that server automatically. How MCP connections work When a customer asks a question, Gladly AI decides whether one of your MCP tools can help. If it can, Gladly AI calls the tool on your MCP server, reads the response, and uses it to answer the customer. For example, a customer asks, "Where is my order RT-1001?" Gladly AI calls an order lookup tool on your server, gets back the status, carrier, and tracking number, and shares them in its reply. Servers, connections, and tools Three terms describe how MCP fits together in Gladly: Server: The external system that offers tools, identified by its URL. For example, an MCP server for your order management system. Connection: How your org connects to a server. A connection has a name, the authentication details for the server, and an active or inactive status. You can create more than one connection to the same server, for example to use different credentials. Tool: A single capability the server offers, such as lookup_order_status or search_products . Each tool has a description and the inputs it needs. Where Gladly AI uses MCP tools MCP tools reach Gladly AI only after you add them to a Guide or Skill. Adding a connection on its own doesn't change how Gladly AI responds. In a Guide, you wrap an MCP tool in a Custom Action, then add that Action to a Guide section. The Custom Action calls the MCP tool as one of its steps, and you control what the Action collects from the customer and what it passes to the tool. MCP tools work alongside your other Actions, so a single Guide can use both. See Set up MCP connections for the steps. Authentication options Gladly supports the following authentication types for an MCP server: None Bearer Token API Key OAuth (Authorization Code) OAuth (Client Credentials) Use the type your server requires. If you're not sure which one to use, ask the team that manages the server. Manage MCP connections You manage connections from Settings , under App Developer Tools , on the MCP page. From there you can: Add a connection to a new or existing server. Test a connection to confirm Gladly can reach the server and find its tools. Run a tool on its own to see what it returns. View tool call logs to see each request and response. Edit, deactivate, or delete a connection. See Set up MCP connections for step-by-step instructions. Things to know Guardrails still apply. Replies that use MCP tool data pass the same reply guardrails as any other Gladly AI reply. Gladly doesn't screen the tool's output itself, so make sure your server returns only information you're comfortable sharing with customers. Tools only. MCP connections support tools. Resources and prompts offered by an MCP server aren't available. If a server is unreachable. Gladly drops only that server's tools for that turn, and the rest of the conversation continues. Everything is logged. Each tool call, including test runs, appears in the connection's tool call logs. Tool calls also appear in conversation history and action logs. Customer or C ustomers refers to the people you support through Gladly who buy or use your products or services. Conversation or Conversations (with a capital "C")  provides a holistic view of Customer communications and interactions contained in the Conversation Timeline. Was this doc helpful?
